title: Branch timeline race
materials: Branch timeline deck per patrol: 24 cards (6 names, 6 founding dates, 6 domains, 6 “what we do”)
A rope per patrol for the timeline

displayContent.headline: Branch timeline race
displayContent.body: Lay your rope on the floor as a timeline. Build one row per branch, oldest first.
points: Domain: land, sea, air, space, coast or sea-to-land
One point per card in the right place

leaderScript: Hand each patrol a shuffled 24-card deck and a rope.
They lay the rope as a timeline and build one row per branch in founding order.
Score one point per correct card. Press R to show the answer key on the projector while you score.
Ask the discussion questions while you score. Question 3 sets up Meeting 2, so just plant it.

discussionQuestions.question: The Army fights on land and the Navy at sea. Why do we also need Marines?
discussionQuestions.answer: Marines specialize in getting from the sea to the land fast to answer a crisis: expeditionary and amphibious operations.

discussionQuestions.question: The Air Force split from the Army in 1947, and the Space Force split from the Air Force in 2019. What pattern do you see? Will there be a seventh branch?
discussionQuestions.answer: A new domain grows big enough to get its own branch. No right answer on a seventh; let them argue (cyber comes up a lot).

discussionQuestions.question: The Coast Guard arrests drug smugglers, but the Army can’t arrest anyone at home. Why the difference?
discussionQuestions.answer: Plant it and leave it open: the Coast Guard is a law enforcement agency, and a law keeps the other branches out of police work. That’s Meeting 2.

discussionQuestions.question: The GPS on your parents’ phones is owned by the Space Force. What else would stop working without it?
discussionQuestions.answer: Open question. Maps and directions are the obvious one; let them think of others.

cells: Fights and holds ground; the largest branch
Controls the seas with carriers, submarines and ships
Law enforcement at sea, search and rescue, port security

ifShortOnTime: Use only the name and date cards (12 per patrol) and ask just discussion question 1.
lowVolunteerNote: One leader can run it: both patrols race at once, and the leader scores with the answer key on screen.
